original.statement: The storage version of clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io changes from v1beta1 to v1 (in chart 0.16.0 the CRD no longer marks v1beta1 as storage, true → false), so existing ClusterExternalSecret objects stay stored as v1beta1 until a storage version migration (re-write all objects) is run and status.storedVersions is updated, which must happen before a later release removes v1beta1.

corrected.statement: The storage version of clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io changes from v1beta1 to v1. Exposed environments are those whose CRD still lists v1beta1 in status.storedVersions: their objects must be rewritten and storedVersions updated before a later release removes v1beta1.

decision.reason: [ev-a93bb3b1d26d] shows that from 0.15.0 to 0.16.0 the clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io CRD changes spec.versions[name=v1beta1].storage from true to false. The change text says existing objects stay stored as v1beta1 until they are rewritten and status.storedVersions is updated. Whether an environment is exposed therefore depends on what is stored, not on which apiVersion its manifests use. Objects created under 0.15.0 are stored as v1beta1 no matter how they are applied, and manifests that still say v1beta1 continue to be served. The canonical CRD-migration condition (status.storedVersions[] contains v1beta1) captures exactly this state, so the gvk-in-use v1beta1 condition is the wrong test.
